rubric.label: Along-road clarity
rubric.description: Can houses, intersections and road edges be understood while advancing? Review the first six seconds; no real-time frame-rate claim.
rubric.anchors: Reviewer anchors: 0 unusable; 2 severe defects; 5 recognizable prototype with obvious defects; 8 mostly clear/stable in reviewed views; 10 close to source quality throughout. Intermediate integers are judgments, not calibrated measurements.

rubric.label: Side-to-side stability
rubric.description: Do facades and poles stay coherent when leaving the capture path? Review seconds 6–10. This is relative view consistency, not surveyed geometry.
rubric.anchors: Reviewer anchors: 0 unusable; 2 severe defects; 5 recognizable prototype with obvious defects; 8 mostly clear/stable in reviewed views; 10 close to source quality throughout. Intermediate integers are judgments, not calibrated measurements.

rubric.label: Detail sharpness
rubric.description: Roof edges, windows, signs and porch detail in the unenhanced browser samples. This is a 960×540 delivery review, not a native-resolution contest.
rubric.anchors: Reviewer anchors: 0 unusable; 2 severe defects; 5 recognizable prototype with obvious defects; 8 mostly clear/stable in reviewed views; 10 close to source quality throughout. Intermediate integers are judgments, not calibrated measurements.

rubric.label: Freedom from artifacts
rubric.description: Fewer ghosts, streaks, transparent smears, dark holes and duplicated objects score higher. Fine temporal flicker is not measured by an 8 fps preview.
rubric.anchors: Reviewer anchors: 0 unusable; 2 severe defects; 5 recognizable prototype with obvious defects; 8 mostly clear/stable in reviewed views; 10 close to source quality throughout. Intermediate integers are judgments, not calibrated measurements.

rubric.label: Coverage & continuity
rubric.description: Continuity across the reviewed route and lateral views. A longer capture does not automatically earn points; hidden backs of buildings and a complete city are not tested.
rubric.anchors: Reviewer anchors: 0 unusable; 2 severe defects; 5 recognizable prototype with obvious defects; 8 mostly clear/stable in reviewed views; 10 close to source quality throughout. Intermediate integers are judgments, not calibrated measurements.

rubric.label: Training speed
rubric.description: Measured model-training stage only. Excludes extraction, camera solving, masking, exports and human review; captures and iteration counts differ.
rubric.anchors: Project preference, linearly interpolated then rounded to 0.5: 5 min or less=10; 30 min=8; 1 h=6; 3 h=4; 6 h=2; 12 h or more=0. Not an end-to-end benchmark.

rubric.label: Effort to repeat
rubric.description: Hands-on setup, correction and review effort. No reliable human-hours log was found for any model; every entry receives the same explicitly unknown neutral placeholder.
rubric.anchors: Unknown=5 neutral, not a measured assessment. A future time diary can replace it. This unresolved category alone could change any total by ±5 points.

rubric.label: Small download
rubric.description: Exact bytes of the currently published 3D model only. Excludes shared viewer code, thumbnails and optional videos. This rates packaging as delivered, not raw training storage or bytes per street metre.
rubric.anchors: Project preference, linear then rounded to 0.5: ≤5 MB=10; 10 MB=9; 15 MB=8; 25 MB=7; 35 MB=6; 50 MB=4; ≥100 MB=0. MB=1,000,000 bytes.

rubric.label: Browser cost proxy
rubric.description: Published splat count is a rough complexity proxy. Does not measure FPS, GPU memory, thermal behavior, overdraw or physical-phone performance.
rubric.anchors: Project preference, linear then rounded to 0.5: ≤250k=10; 500k=8; 750k=6; 1M=4; 1.5M=2; ≥2M=0.

rubric.label: Evidence & repeatability
rubric.description: Availability of hashed artifacts, saved camera paths, settings, timing and comparisons. More evidence raises confidence, not image quality.
rubric.anchors: 5=hashed model and repeatable browser samples; 6=plus useful runtime/status; 7=plus source/native metrics; 8=plus paired or independently documented native motion review. No entry earns 10: no independent off-path geometry truth or repeated-run uncertainty.

methodology.scope: Provisional ratings of 21 currently published Gaussian assets. Higher is better. Visual quality counts for 65%; training time and effort 20%; model download 10%; browser cost proxy and evidence 5%. No model is certified as a finished street.
methodology.formula: Total = round(sum(category score / 10 × category weight)). Equal rounded totals share a rank; no forced winner. Visual subtotal is out of 65.
methodology.unknownPolicy: Unknown effort=5/10 neutral for every model; missing complete training time=5/10 neutral. These are placeholders, not measurements. Unknown effort alone can move a total ±5 points (±10 when time is also unknown), before subjective-review uncertainty. Treat close ranks as unresolved.
comparisonLimits: Compare the same-footage groups before drawing method conclusions. Global scores include different capture lengths, camera paths, lighting, training budgets and packaging.
Human hours, complete pipeline time, surveyed accuracy, mobile FPS and GPU memory are unknown. Count is only a browser-cost proxy.
Scores and utility anchors express this project’s priorities, not an industry standard or probability of success. Small score differences do not establish a robust winner.
The published PLY diagnostics are larger than SOG models. Repacking may improve download rank without changing training quality.
Source-view PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS measure image fit; they do not certify side-to-side geometry. Single runs and shared SfM observations limit inference.
The broader off-path experiment was still evolving. These ratings cover only the 21 published hashes, not later results.
methodology.previewProtocol: Each model has a 960×540, 75° field-of-view, 80-frame review encoded at 8 fps: 0–6s along the route, 6–10s lateral. Review duration is not capture duration. Eight labelled samples plus 1:1 center crops support the written observations. No enhancement was applied. Camera paths match within the listed groups; original-turn/MRNF lateral offsets are arbitrary reconstruction units, not measured lane widths. Compressed previews and sparse sampling cannot measure high-frequency flicker or live performance.
